The test image shows a soybean root/lower stem with distinctive **blue-green fungal sporulation** covering the root surface. This is the hallmark diagnostic feature of Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS), caused by *Fusarium virguliforme*.

Key observations:
- Blue-green spore mass on the taproot surface
- Rotted/degraded root tissue
- The SDS reference collage (bottom-left) shows a very similar root presentation
- The symptom description explicitly states: "Bluish fungal growth may appear on root surfaces under high soil moisture. Blue-green spores of the fungus can occasionally be seen on the tap root after rain."

This rules out Charcoal Rot (black microsclerotia, no blue), Fusarium wilt (brown vascular tissue but no blue sporulation), and White Mold (white fluffy mycelium with black sclerotia).
